modern:
This is the first promise God ever gave to fallen humanity. It holds the whole gospel, the very heart of the covenant of grace. Much of it has already come true. The woman’s offspring, our Lord Jesus, was bruised in his heel, and it was a terrible bruising. But how terrible the final crushing of the serpent’s head will be! In effect, that happened when Jesus took away sin, defeated death and broke Satan’s power. But it still waits to be fulfilled even more fully when our Lord comes again, and on the Day of Judgment.

For us, the promise is a prophecy that the powers of evil will trouble us in our lower nature, and so bruise our heel. But we’ll triumph in Christ, who sets his foot on the old serpent’s head. This year we may have to learn the first part of the promise the hard way, through the devil’s temptations and the unkindness of the ungodly, who are his offspring. They may bruise us so badly that we limp on a sore heel. But let’s hold tight to the second part of the verse, and we won’t lose heart. By faith, let’s be glad that we’ll still reign in Christ Jesus, the woman’s offspring.

notes.note: Humanity after Adam and Eve’s first sin ([[Gen.3.6|Genesis 3:6]]).
God’s binding promise to save his people through Christ, freely, as a gift and not a reward.
Offspring, descendants. “Her seed” points to Christ, “made of a woman” ([[Gal.4.4|Galatians 4:4]]). The “seed” of the serpent is everyone who sides with the devil.
In the King James Bible, a stronger word than today’s: to crush or wound.
In effect, in all that matters (not “almost”).
Christ’s second coming. “Advent” means a coming or arrival.
Satan, “that old serpent, called the Devil” ([[Rev.12.9|Revelation 12:9]]).

modern: This promise follows well on yesterday’s. Clearly we’re meant to become like Christ, the Head of our covenant, not only in having our heel bruised as he did, but in his victory over the evil one too. The old dragon is to be crushed even under our feet. The believers in Rome were upset by quarrels in their church, but their God was “the God of peace,” and he gave them rest in their souls. Their great enemy tripped up the careless and fooled the simple, but he would come off worst, trampled by the very people he had troubled. This victory wouldn’t come to God’s people through their own skill or strength. God himself would crush Satan. It would happen under their feet, yet the crushing would be the Lord’s work alone.

Let’s bravely trample the tempter! Not just lesser spirits, but the Prince of darkness himself has to go down before us. Trusting God without question, let’s look for a quick victory. “SHORTLY.” What a happy word! Soon we’ll put our foot on the old serpent! What a joy to crush evil! What a disgrace for Satan to have his head crushed by human feet! By faith in Jesus, let’s tread the tempter down.

notes.note: Made to match, shaped to be like. God’s people are “conformed to the image of his Son” ([[Rom.8.29|Romans 8:29]]).
Christ, who stands at the head of God’s covenant for all his people, as Adam stood for all humanity ([[Rom.5.19|Romans 5:19]]). What happened to the Head happens to his people.
Satan ([[Rev.12.9|Revelation 12:9]]).
Chief enemy.
Soon. Spurgeon lifts the word from the day’s text and shouts it.

modern: No promise belongs to just one person. It isn’t for one saint only, but for every believer. My friend, if by faith you can lie down on a promise and rest on it, it’s yours. Where Jacob “lighted,” and stayed, and rested, he took possession. As he stretched his tired body out on the ground, with stones from that place for his pillows, he hardly imagined he was becoming the owner of the land. Yet he was. In his dream he saw that wonderful ladder which, for every true believer, joins earth and heaven. And surely he had a right to the ground where the foot of the ladder stood, or he couldn’t have reached the stairway to God. All God’s promises are Yes and Amen in Christ Jesus. And since he is ours, every promise is ours, if only we’ll lie down on it in restful faith.

Come, you who are tired, use your Lord’s words as your pillows. Lie down in peace. Dream only of him. Jesus is your ladder of light. See the angels going up and down on him, between your soul and your God. And be sure that the promise is your own God-given share, and that it won’t be stealing to take it for yourself, as if it had been spoken just to you.

notes.note: An echo of [[2Pet.1.20|2 Peter 1:20]]. Here it means no promise is the private property of one person.
Came upon, stopped at. “He lighted upon a certain place” ([[Gen.28.11|Genesis 28:11]]).

Jacob’s dream at Bethel ([[Gen.28.12|Genesis 28:12]]). Jesus later said the angels would ascend and descend “upon the Son of man” ([[John.1.51|John 1:51]]), which is why Spurgeon calls Jesus the ladder.
Yes and amen: certain and settled. “All the promises of God in him are yea, and in him Amen” ([[2Cor.1.20|2 Corinthians 1:20]]).
A share of an inheritance.

modern: Yes, God’s people are going to have peace. The passage this gracious word comes from speaks of peace “with the beasts of the field, and with the fowls of heaven, and with the creeping things of the ground.” That means peace with earthly enemies, with mysterious evils and with small irritations! Any of these could keep us from lying down, but none of them will. The Lord will completely destroy whatever threatens his people: “I will break the bow and the sword, and the battle out of the earth.” Peace will be deep indeed when every tool of unrest has been smashed to pieces.
With this peace will come rest. “So he giveth his beloved sleep.” Fully provided for and quieted by God himself, believers lie down in calm rest.

And this rest will be safe. It’s one thing to lie down, but quite another “to lie down safely.” We’ve been brought to the promised land, the Father’s house, the room of love, close against Christ’s heart. Surely now we can “lie down safely.” It’s safer for a believer to lie down in peace than to sit up and worry.
“He maketh me to lie down in green pastures.” We never rest until the Comforter makes us lie down.

notes.note: Rest.
Birds of any kind, not only farm poultry.
Unrest, anxiety.
The chest, the place of closest embrace. The disciple Jesus loved leaned on his bosom at the Last Supper ([[John.13.23|John 13:23]]).

notes.term: “He maketh me to lie down in green pastures”

notes.note: The Holy Spirit; Jesus’ name for him in [[John.14.26|John 14:26]].

modern: When we’re called to serve or to suffer, we take stock of our strength, and we find we have less than we thought, and less than we need. But don’t let your heart sink while you have a word like this to fall back on, because it guarantees everything we could possibly need. God has unlimited strength. He can pass that strength on to us, and he promises that he will. He’ll be the food of our souls and the health of our hearts, and that’s how he’ll make us strong. There’s no telling how much power God can put into a person. When God’s strength comes, human weakness is no longer a problem.

Don’t we remember times of hard work and trial when we were given such special strength that we amazed ourselves? In danger we were calm. In grief we accepted God’s will. Under slander we kept our self-control, and in sickness we were patient. The fact is, God gives unexpected strength when unusual trials come. We rise above our feeble selves. Cowards act like heroes, foolish people are given wisdom, and the quiet ones are given what to say in the very hour they need it. My own weakness makes me shrink back, but God’s promise makes me brave. Lord, strengthen me “according to thy word.”

notes.note: All-powerful.
Losing someone close through death.
In Spurgeon’s sense, quietly accepting God’s will, not giving up.
Calm and in control of ourselves.
Act with courage.
Jesus promised that when his followers were put on trial, “it shall be given you in that same hour what ye shall speak” ([[Matt.10.19|Matthew 10:19]]).
A prayer from [[Ps.119.28|Psalm 119:28]], “strengthen thou me according unto thy word.”

modern: Yesterday’s promise made sure of our strength for what we have to do. This one guarantees us help when we can’t manage alone. The Lord says, “I will help thee.” The strength he gives inside us is backed up by help from outside. God can raise up allies for us in our battles if he thinks it good. And even if he doesn’t send us human help, he himself will be at our side, and that’s better still. “Our August Ally” is better than armies of human helpers.

His help comes right on time: he’s always there when trouble comes. His help is wise: he knows how to give each person exactly the help that suits them. His help really works, even though human help is useless. His help is more than help, because he carries the whole burden and supplies every need. “The Lord is my helper, I will not fear what man can do unto me.”

Because he has already been our help, we trust him for now and for what’s ahead. Our prayer is, “Lord, be thou my helper”; our experience is, “The Spirit also helpeth our infirmities”; our hope is, “I will lift up mine eyes unto the hills, whence cometh my help”; and soon our song will be, “Thou, Lord, hast holpen me.”

notes.note: Outside. “Help from without” is help from outside ourselves.
Grand, majestic, worthy of honor (not the month).
From [[Ps.46.1|Psalm 46:1]], “God is our refuge and strength, a very present help in trouble.”
Suitable, fitting.
Effective; actually doing what it sets out to do.

notes.term: Vain is the help of man
notes.note: From [[Ps.60.11|Psalm 60:11]]. “Vain” means useless.
[[Heb.13.6|Hebrews 13:6]].
Weaknesses ([[Rom.8.26|Romans 8:26]]).
An old form of “helped” ([[Ps.86.17|Psalm 86:17]]).

modern: This was said to a believer with childlike faith, who was ready to accept Jesus as the Son of God and the King of Israel on the strength of one convincing proof. Those who are willing to see will see. It’s because we shut our eyes that we end up so sadly blind.

We’ve already seen a lot. The Lord has shown us great things, too great to search out, and we praise his name for them. But there are greater truths in his Word, deeper experiences, higher heights of fellowship, greater works of service, and greater discoveries of power and love and wisdom. We have yet to see these, if we’re willing to believe our Lord. Inventing false teaching does terrible damage, but the ability to see the truth is a blessing. Heaven will be opened to us. The way there will be made clear to us in the Son of man. And the coming and going of angels between the higher and lower worlds will be shown to us more plainly. Let’s keep our eyes open to spiritual things and expect to see more and more. Let’s believe that our lives won’t dribble away into nothing, but that we’ll always be growing, seeing greater and still greater things, until we see the great God himself and never lose sight of him again.

notes.note: Nathanael, who believed after Jesus told him he had seen him under the fig tree ([[John.1.48-John.1.49|John 1:48–49]]).
Too great to be fully searched out. From [[Job.5.9|Job 5:9]], “Which doeth great things and unsearchable.”
An ability or power of the mind.

“Commerce” once meant any coming and going or exchange, not only trade. Jesus promised Nathanael he would see “the angels of God ascending and descending upon the Son of man” ([[John.1.51|John 1:51]]).
Dribble away, trickle off into nothing.
An old phrase for “on the increase,” always growing.
